Sofia / Tom — great, thanks for the quick turnaround. A few notes and attachments to unblock your compliance review: 

1) SOC 2 package: I'm attaching our SOC 2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary.pdf). We can provide the full auditor report under NDA — if you want that I'll route it via our security team and send a short NDA link.

2) BAA / HIPAA: We support HIPAA-covered workflows and have BAA language we can share; Monica will coordinate the legal/BAA questions with your counsel.

3) Deployment options (high level): 
- Hosted-in-VPC (recommended): Redwood runs inference in a customer VPC with VPC peering or Transit Gateway; customer-managed KMS for envelope keys, VPC flow logs to your logging account, private endpoints only.
- Dedicated private: 100% dedicated GPU pool deployed in your cloud account with stricter tenancy and no multi-tenant control plane access.
- On-prem / air-gapped: Appliance or container bundle deployed behind your firewall with one-way sync for model updates (optional), no outbound egress required. Requires ops automation and periodic secure media for updates.

4) Network & security controls we'll implement for each option: TLS mutual auth, mTLS for control plane, role-based access controls, token-level audit logs, customer-managed KMS support, configurable data retention and purge hooks.

5) Next step: Monica (cc) will own drafting the deployment diagram and a short checklist we can share with your infra team (Tom). Monica — can you pull the VPC-onprem checklist and propose a diagram by EOD?

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf, vpc-onprem-checklist.docx

Tom / Sofia — following Marcus's note, I'm attaching a first draft of the deployment diagram and a short checklist. High-level technical notes below (copied into the doc and summarized here):

- For Hosted-in-VPC: we recommend using a separate customer VPC with private subnets for inference nodes and a dedicated NAT/egress path only to your logging and metrics endpoints. Use VPC peering or TGW, and enforce security groups that restrict egress to the minimal set (KMS endpoints, logging).
- KMS: Customer-managed KMS is supported. We recommend envelope encryption where the customer KMS wraps the model keys; Redwood does not persist unencrypted model secrets.
- Networking: Support for static CIDR allocations or BGP peering for on-prem connections. If you require air-gapped, we propose an offline media update process or a one-way data diode for model sync.
- Audit: Token-level audit logs shipped to your secure bucket with configurable retention (we can set to 12 months or longer).

Request from you: please share the following before the deep-dive so I can finalize the diagram:
- Preferred private CIDR(s) and whether you use TGW (yes/no)
- Any outbound egress restrictions or proxy requirements for software updates
- Contact for legal to discuss BAA (if applicable)

Drive link for diagram and checklist: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123-redwood-diagrams

I'll turn this into a runnable checklist and a technical appendix to the questionnaire after your responses.

Thanks — Monica Patel
